system.summary: The Grand Chiffre de 1691: a numeric nomenclator of 587 groups for letters, CV syllables, word stems, whole words and nulls.
system.sibling_key: Bazeries' reconstruction of the Grand Chiffre (../feuquieres/grand_chiffre_1691.tsv, 587 entries, 91 blank), used as the key.
system.notes: Six groups printed above 587 in 1819 and one damaged glyph stay unread; about a hundred groups fall on entries Bazeries left blank and are read from context.

prior_solution.where: Bazeries 1893 printed L1 and L3 in clear and parts of L2 and L4; L5-L7 never printed in clear

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: segment.py (dynamic-programming word segmenter over a period lexicon)

solution.what: Fetched MDZ hOCR and IIIF page images of Mémoires de Catinat t. II.
Tokenised the figures from the hOCR, dropping specks, running heads and show-through glyphs; split into seven letters.
Applied Bazeries' 1893 Grand Chiffre table and segmented the output with a period lexicon.
Aligned the decode of L1 and L3 with Bazeries' clear text: 98.1% and 99.1% of characters.
Checked 137 doubtful stretches on page crops; 7 OCR errors and 3 dates corrected.
Read all seven letters, five of them for the first time in print.

outcome.method_basis: Bazeries' 1893 reconstruction of the Grand Chiffre (Le Masque de fer), built from these very Catinat despatches, was applied to OCR'd figures from the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat; Bazeries' clear texts of L1 and L3 served as controls (98.1% and 99.1%).
outcome.notes: Seven groups unread (six misprinted above 587, one damaged); about a hundred blank-table groups read from context.
